info.title: Ambivo Agents SDK
info.description:
## Overview

The **Ambivo Agents SDK** is a Python SDK for orchestrating AI agents. It provides
**15 specialized agents** with a unified chat interface, SSE streaming, Redis-backed
session memory, and multi-provider LLM support (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock).

Every agent inherits from `BaseAgent` and exposes a consistent `chat()` / `chat_sync()`
interface. The `ModeratorAgent` acts as an intelligent router, automatically dispatching
queries to the most appropriate specialist agent.

## Installation

```bash
pip install ambivo-agents[all]
```

Extras: `[web]` (web search/scraping), `[media]` (FFmpeg processing), `[test]` (pytest deps).

## Quick Start

```python
from ambivo_agents.agents.moderator import ModeratorAgent

moderator = ModeratorAgent.create_simple(user_id="user-123")

# Auto-routes to the best specialist agent
response = await moderator.chat("Search the web for AI news")
print(response.content)

await moderator.cleanup_session()
```

## Authentication

All HTTP endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.

## Response Pattern

Every agent returns an **AgentMessage** with standard metadata:

```json
{
  "id": "msg-uuid",
  "content": "The agent's response text",
  "metadata": {
    "agent_id": "moderator-abc123",
    "agent_type": "moderator",
    "session_id": "sess-xyz",
    "streaming_supported": true
  },
  "message_type": "agent_response",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-21T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## SSE Streaming Protocol

Streaming endpoints return `text/event-stream` with the following event types:

| Event Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `stream_start` | Stream opened; includes agent metadata |
| `stream_chunk` | Incremental content token |
| `stream_status` | Progress or status update |
| `stream_complete` | Final message with full metadata |
| `stream_error` | Error during streaming |
| `stream_cancelled` | Client or server cancelled the stream |
| `keepalive` | Heartbeat to keep the connection alive |

Example SSE frame:
```
event: stream_chunk
data: {"type":"stream_chunk","text":"Hello","sub_type":"content","timestamp":"2026-03-21T12:00:00Z"}
```

## Configuration

Agents are configured via **`agent_config.yaml`** (auto-loaded when `auto_configure=True`)
or through environment variables prefixed with `AMBIVO_AGENTS_`:

```bash
export AMBIVO_AGENTS_REDIS_HOST="localhost"
export AMBIVO_AGENTS_OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
```

## Agent Inventory

| # | Agent | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ModeratorAgent | Intelligent query router and orchestrator |
| 2 | AssistantAgent | General-purpose conversational AI |
| 3 | CodeExecutorAgent | Secure Python/Bash execution in Docker |
| 4 | WebSearchAgent | Multi-provider web search (Brave, AVES) |
| 5 | KnowledgeBaseAgent | Document ingestion and semantic search (Qdrant) |
| 6 | KnowledgeSynthesisAgent | Multi-source knowledge orchestration |
| 7 | ResponseQualityAssessor | Response quality evaluation and scoring |
| 8 | MediaEditorAgent | FFmpeg-based audio/video/image processing |
| 9 | YouTubeDownloadAgent | YouTube content downloading via Docker |
| 10 | WebScraperAgent | Playwright-based web scraping in Docker |
| 11 | AnalyticsAgent | DuckDB data analysis and visualization |
| 12 | DatabaseAgent | MongoDB/MySQL/PostgreSQL operations |
| 13 | APIAgent | REST API integration with security controls |
| 14 | GatherAgent | Conversational form-filling with conditional logic |
| 15 | WorkflowDeveloperAgent | Guided workflow code generation |

tags.name: ModeratorAgent
tags.description:
Intelligent orchestrator that routes queries to specialized agents.
Performs intent analysis using both LLM reasoning and keyword patterns,
maintains conversation context across agent switches, and supports
workflow execution and multi-agent coordination. This is the primary
entry point for most use cases.

tags.name: AssistantAgent
tags.description:
General-purpose conversational AI agent for explanations, summaries,
brainstorming, and any query that does not require a specialist tool.
Acts as the default fallback when the ModeratorAgent cannot match
a specialist.

tags.name: CodeExecutorAgent
tags.description:
Executes Python and Bash code in isolated Docker containers with
network isolation, memory limits, and timeout controls. Default image:
`sgosain/amb-ubuntu-python-public-pod`. Containers are automatically
cleaned up after execution.

tags.name: WebSearchAgent
tags.description:
Multi-provider web search supporting Brave Search and AVES APIs.
Returns ranked search results with titles, URLs, and snippets.
Provider failover is automatic.

tags.name: KnowledgeBaseAgent
tags.description:
Document ingestion and semantic search powered by Qdrant vector
database. Supports ingesting files (PDF, TXT, DOCX, CSV, JSON) and
URLs, then querying with natural-language semantic search.

tags.name: KnowledgeSynthesisAgent
tags.description:
Multi-source knowledge orchestration agent that synthesizes information
from multiple agents and knowledge bases. Supports configurable synthesis
strategies and integrates with the ResponseQualityAssessor for quality
evaluation of synthesized outputs.

tags.name: ResponseQualityAssessor
tags.description:
Evaluates and scores the quality of agent responses. Assesses accuracy,
completeness, relevance, and source coverage. Returns a structured
assessment with quality level, confidence score, strengths, weaknesses,
and improvement recommendations.

tags.name: MediaEditorAgent
tags.description:
FFmpeg-based media processing agent for audio, video, and image
operations. Runs in Docker for isolation. Supports trimming, merging,
format conversion, audio extraction, and filter application.

tags.name: YouTubeDownloadAgent
tags.description:
Downloads YouTube content via pytubefix running in Docker containers.
Supports audio-only extraction, format selection, and custom output
filenames.

tags.name: WebScraperAgent
tags.description:
Playwright-based web scraping agent running in Docker. Extracts text
content, links, images, and can take full-page screenshots. Supports
proxy configuration and JavaScript rendering.

tags.name: AnalyticsAgent
tags.description:
Data analysis agent powered by DuckDB. Loads CSV, XLSX, JSON, and
Parquet files, then answers natural-language queries by generating
and executing SQL. Supports visualization recommendations and schema
inspection.

tags.name: DatabaseAgent
tags.description:
Connects to MongoDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL databases. Translates
natural-language questions into database queries, executes them, and
returns structured results.

tags.name: APIAgent
tags.description:
REST API integration agent with configurable security controls.
Parses natural-language API call descriptions, supports Bearer, Basic,
and API-key authentication, and routes long-running requests through
Docker for safety.

tags.name: GatherAgent
tags.description:
Conversational form-filling agent with conditional question logic.
Drives a guided questionnaire session, supporting free-text, yes/no,
single-select, and multi-select question types with parent-dependent
branching.

tags.name: WorkflowDeveloperAgent
tags.description:
Guided workflow code generation agent. Accepts a natural-language
description of a multi-agent workflow and produces executable Python
code using the SDK's workflow system (sequential, parallel, consensus,
debate, and map-reduce patterns).

AgentMessage.description: Standard response envelope returned by every agent.

sender_id.description: Agent ID that produced this message.

content.description: The main text body of the response.
content.example: Here are the latest AI news articles I found...

message_type.description: Discriminator indicating the kind of message.

metadata.description:
Standard metadata plus agent-specific keys. Every response
includes at least `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `session_id`, and
`streaming_supported`.

conversation_id.description: Specific conversation thread within the session.

StreamChunk.description: A single frame in an SSE streaming response.

text.example: The answer to your question is

sub_type.description: Further classification of the chunk payload.

metadata.description: Additional context (agent info, token counts, etc.).

CreateAgentRequest.description: Request body to instantiate an agent.

user_id.description: Unique identifier for the calling user.

session_id.description:
Optional existing session ID to resume. If omitted the server
generates a new session.

system_message.description: Custom system prompt that overrides the agent's default.
system_message.example: You are a helpful data analyst.

auto_configure.description:
When true (default) the agent loads configuration from
`agent_config.yaml` or environment variables automatically.

agent_id.description: Unique identifier for the newly created agent instance.

session_id.description: The session ID assigned (new or resumed).

ChatRequest.description: Send a message to an agent.

message.example: What are the latest trends in AI?

session_id.description: Session to use. Must match a previously created agent session.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs forwarded to the agent.

content.example: Here are the latest AI trends...

metadata.description: Standard agent metadata plus any agent-specific keys.

APIRequest.description:
Describes an outbound HTTP request to be executed by the APIAgent.
Requests with timeout exceeding `max_safe_timeout` (default 8s) are
routed through Docker for safety.

url.description: Target URL for the API call.

api_key.description: API key value (sent via header or query).

timeout.description:
Request timeout in seconds. Values above `max_safe_timeout` (default 8)
cause the request to execute inside a Docker container.

APIResponse.description: Result of an outbound API request.

status_code.description: HTTP status code from the target server.

size_bytes.description: Size of the response body in bytes.

success.description: True if the request completed without transport errors.

query.example: latest advances in large language models 2026

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return.

provider.description: Preferred search provider. If omitted, the agent selects automatically.

snippet.example: This survey covers the latest breakthroughs in...

query.example: latest advances in large language models 2026

total_results.description: Total results available from the provider.

IngestRequest.description: Request to ingest documents into a knowledge base collection.

kb_name.description: Name of the knowledge base collection in Qdrant.

documents.description: List of file paths or URLs to ingest.

custom_meta.description: Extra metadata attached to every ingested chunk.

IngestResponse.description: Result of a document ingestion operation.

KBQueryRequest.description: Semantic search query against a knowledge base.

top_k.description: Number of top results to return.

port.description: Port number (defaults to the engine's standard port).

ssl.description: Whether to use SSL/TLS for the connection.

DatabaseQueryRequest.description: A query to execute against the connected database.

query.description: Natural-language question or raw SQL/MQL query.
query.example: What are the top 10 customers by revenue?

QueryResult.description: Result of a database query execution.

error.description: Error message if the query failed.

ExecuteCodeRequest.description: Request to execute code in an isolated Docker container.

files.description:
Files to mount into the container. Keys are filenames, values
are file contents.

files_created.description: List of output files created by the script.

ProcessMediaRequest.description: Media processing request via FFmpeg in Docker.

input_file.description: Path to the input media file.

operation.description:
Processing operation to perform (e.g., trim, merge, convert,
extract_audio, apply_filter, resize).

output_file.description: Path to the generated output file.

title.example: Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up

extract_links.description: Extract all hyperlinks from the page.

extract_images.description: Extract all image URLs from the page.

text_content.description: Extracted text content from the page.

screenshot_path.description: Path to screenshot file if requested.

LoadAnalyticsRequest.description: Load a data file for analysis.

file_path.description:
Path to the data file. Relative paths are resolved against
`docker_shared/input/analytics/` first.

file_type.description: Explicit file type override (auto-detected from extension by default).

LoadAnalyticsResponse.description: Summary returned after loading a data file.

AnalyticsQueryRequest.description: Natural-language or SQL query against loaded data.

query.example: What are the top 10 products by revenue?

sql_generated.description: The SQL query that was generated and executed.
sql_generated.example: SELECT product, SUM(revenue) as total FROM sales GROUP BY product ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10

GatherQuestion.description: A single question in a questionnaire definition.

text.description: The question text shown to the user.
text.example: What is your preferred programming language?

choices.description: Available choices (for single-select and multi-select types).

condition.description:
Conditional display logic. The question is shown only when the
parent question's answer matches one of the trigger values.

trigger_values.description: Parent answer values that activate this question.

GatherRespondRequest.description: Submit an answer to the current question.

answers_collected.description: All answers collected so far (keyed by question ID).

query.description: The question or topic to synthesize information about.
query.example: Compare transformer architectures for sequence modeling

AssessRequest.description: Request to assess the quality of one or more responses.

question.description: The original question that was asked.
question.example: Explain the CAP theorem in distributed systems.

responses.description: List of source responses to evaluate.

source.description: Name or ID of the responding agent/source.

ResponseAssessment.description: Structured quality assessment of a response.

confidence_score.description: Confidence in the assessment (0.0 = no confidence, 1.0 = fully confident).

sources_used.description: Sources that contributed to the evaluated response.

weaknesses.description: Areas where the response falls short.

example: Add real-world examples from industry databases

needs_additional_sources.description: Whether more sources should be consulted.

final_response.example: The CAP theorem, formulated by Eric Brewer...

description.description: Natural-language description of the desired workflow.
description.example: Search the web for a topic, scrape the top 3 results, and ingest them into a knowledge base

agents_needed.description: Specific agents to include in the workflow.

code.description: Executable Python code using the SDK workflow system.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the generated workflow.

pattern.description: Workflow pattern used (sequential, parallel, consensus, debate, map-reduce).

RouteQueryRequest.description: Request the ModeratorAgent to classify and route a query.

query.example: Download audio from this YouTube video

target_agent.description: Agent type selected to handle the query.

reasoning.example: Query contains YouTube URL and requests audio download.

post.summary: Create a ModeratorAgent instance
post.description:
Instantiate a new ModeratorAgent that can route queries to any of
the 14 specialist agents. The moderator maintains conversation
context across agent switches.

post.summary: Send a message to the ModeratorAgent
post.description:
Send a natural-language message. The moderator analyzes intent and
routes to the best specialist agent, returning the specialist's
response with routing metadata.

example.message: Search the web for the latest AI research papers

example.content: Here are the latest AI research papers I found...

post.summary: SSE streaming chat with the ModeratorAgent
post.description:
Stream a response from the ModeratorAgent via Server-Sent Events.
The stream emits `stream_start`, `stream_chunk`, `stream_status`,
and `stream_complete` events.

post.summary: Route a query to a specialist agent
post.description:
Classify a query and return the routing decision without executing
the query. Useful for previewing which agent would handle a message.

example.query: Download audio from this YouTube video

example.reasoning: Query contains YouTube URL and requests audio download.

post.summary: Create an AssistantAgent instance
post.description:
Instantiate a general-purpose conversational AI agent for
explanations, summaries, brainstorming, and general Q&A.

example.system_message: You are a helpful technical writer.

post.summary: Send a message to the AssistantAgent
post.description:
Send a conversational message and receive a response. The assistant
handles general knowledge questions, explanations, writing tasks,
and any query that does not require a specialist tool.

example.message: Explain the difference between TCP and UDP

post.summary: SSE streaming chat with the AssistantAgent

post.description:
Instantiate a code execution agent backed by isolated Docker

Execute Python or Bash code in an isolated Docker container.

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

Send a natural-language search request. The agent selects the best

Instantiate a knowledge base agent backed by Qdrant vector database.

Query the knowledge base using natural language. The agent performs

Evaluate the quality of one or more responses to a given question.

example.question: Explain the CAP theorem in distributed systems.

responses.content: The CAP theorem states that a distributed system can only guarantee two of three properties: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance.

example.description: Search the web for a topic, scrape the top 3 results, and ingest them into a knowledge base

example.code:
from ambivo_agents.core.workflow import Workflow, WorkflowStep
from ambivo_agents.agents.web_search import WebSearchAgent
from ambivo_agents.agents.web_scraper import WebScraperAgent
from ambivo_agents.agents.knowledge_base import KnowledgeBaseAgent

async def search_scrape_ingest(topic: str, kb_name: str):
    search_agent = WebSearchAgent.create_simple(user_id="wf-user")
    scraper_agent = WebScraperAgent.create_simple(user_id="wf-user")
    kb_agent = KnowledgeBaseAgent.create_simple(user_id="wf-user")

    # Step 1: Search
    results = await search_agent.chat(f"Search for {topic}")
    # Step 2: Scrape top 3
    urls = extract_urls(results.content)[:3]
    for url in urls:
        scraped = await scraper_agent.chat(f"Scrape {url}")
    # Step 3: Ingest
    await kb_agent.chat(f"Ingest scraped content into {kb_name}")

    await search_agent.cleanup_session()
    await scraper_agent.cleanup_session()
    await kb_agent.cleanup_session()
example.description: Sequential workflow: web search -> scrape top 3 results -> ingest into knowledge base
